findings.title: Third-party identity provider users blocked from backup code login
findings.body: The authorize callback throws `ErrorCode.ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` for any user whose `identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL` when `credentials.totpCode` is empty. Since the backup-code submission path intentionally leaves `totpCode` empty, Google/SAML users with 2FA enabled cannot authenticate via a backup code even though the rest of the flow (decrypt codes, match, invalidate) was clearly written to support them. The guard needs `!credentials.backupCode` added (or the backup-code branch should run before this check) so non-CAL users can actually use their backup codes.

findings.title: Lost access button hidden for external (third-party) TOTP users
findings.body: The footer for the 2FA-required state branches on `!totpEmail`: only CAL users get `TwoFactorFooter` (which contains the new `lost_access` button that flips `twoFactorLostAccess`). External TOTP users (Google/SAML arriving via the `?totp=` JWT) get `ExternalTotpFooter` (a single Cancel button) and therefore have no way to switch the form to the `BackupCode` input. Combined with the authorize-callback bug, this means users who authenticated via an identity provider and lost their authenticator are locked out with no recovery path.

findings.title: Continue button fires both handleSetup and handleEnable on click
findings.body: The ConfirmPassword `Continue` button is rendered inside `<Form handleSubmit={handleEnable}>` and has both `type="submit"` and `onClick={handleSetup}`. Clicking it triggers (1) `handleSetup` directly via `onClick`, then (2) the surrounding form submission which invokes `handleEnable` via react-hook-form. Because `setIsSubmitting(true)` inside `handleSetup` is not visible to `handleEnable`'s closure until the next render, `handleEnable`'s `isSubmitting` guard does not stop the second call. The setup API and the enable API (with an empty `totpCode`, producing `IncorrectTwoFactorCode`) are both hit, which can display a spurious error and cause the TOTP enable request to race with the step transition. Remove `onClick={handleSetup}` (or change the button to `type="button"`) so only one handler runs.

findings.title: backupCodesUrl object URL is never revoked (blob memory leak)
findings.body: `handleSetup` calls `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` to build the download link for the backup codes, but neither `resetState` nor the component unmount path revokes the previously created URL. The only revocation in the file is `if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);` inside `handleSetup`, which only runs when the user starts setup again. Closing/cancelling the modal or finishing the flow without re-entering setup leaves the blob URL pinned in memory until the page is unloaded. Revoke the URL in `resetState` and in a `useEffect` cleanup function.

findings.title: Backup code comparison is case-sensitive but codes are lowercase hex
findings.body: Backup codes are generated as `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` (lowercase). The match is `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`, which is a strict string equality check. The login UI placeholder (`XXXXX-XXXXX`) and the format function do not normalize case, so a user typing an uppercase or mixed-case backup code (e.g. copied from a notes app that auto-capitalizes) gets `IncorrectBackupCode` even though the code is correct. Normalize both sides to lower case (or uppercase) before comparing, both here and in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` at line 61.

findings.title: formatBackupCode used before its const declaration
findings.body: `handleSetup` references `formatBackupCode` at line 95, but `formatBackupCode` is declared with `const` at line 163 (after `handleSetup`). It happens to work at runtime because the function body is only executed after the component has rendered and `const` initialization has completed, but it is order-dependent and fragile. Move the `const formatBackupCode = ...` declaration above `handleSetup` (or hoist it with a function declaration) so the dependency is explicit and the module doesn't rely on TDZ luck.

findings.title: BackupCode component exported under the name TwoFactor
findings.body: The new file `apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx` declares `export default function TwoFactor(...)`, so every import (`import BackupCode from "@components/auth/BackupCode"`) uses a name that does not match the function it points at. This is confusing to maintainers and also defeats React DevTools / stack-trace readability. Rename the function to `BackupCode` (and update the other call sites: `DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx` line 8, `login.tsx` line 32).
